result:
I fixed the 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings. A script now checks all 150 rules against what their docstrings say, across many quantities and unit prices, and finds no mismatches.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | Capped the price before taking 5%, instead of capping the discount | 5% of the full price, then cap the discount at 30,000 |
| 15, 124 | Labelled "whole" but only discounted units above the threshold | Discount the full amount |
| 27 | Started at 101 units | Starts at 100 units |
| 40, 55 | Cap only applied once the discount passed a higher amount | Cap always applies |
| 46 | Took 4% off | Takes 3% off |
| 59 | Took 3% off | Takes 2% off |
| 47 | Rounded the discount | Rounds it down to the won |
| 106, 107 | Started one unit above the threshold (`>`) | Start at the threshold (`>=`) |

I also changed rule 136 from `>` to `>=` to match. This doesn't change any result: its discount only counts units above 5, so at exactly 5 units it's 0 either way.

STATUS: DONE
